source.title: What do near-optimal learning rate schedules look like?
source.authors: Hiroki Naganuma; Atish Agarwala; Priya Kasimbeg; George E. Dahl

record.tranche_reason: The study varies learning-rate schedule families and reports held-out test metrics on natural CIFAR-10 and WikiText-103 data, but it does not test any claim version about random-label memorization, width, architecture, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper studies schedule shapes and training outcomes, not the train–test generalization gap. It reports test metrics for schedules selected on test metrics; those results bear on the broad claim subject but fit none of the mapped versions. Other results are training metrics or cited prior work.
record.test_reason: The study compares learning-rate schedule shapes, not any intervention or relationship named in V1–V8. Its neural-network experiments use AdamW with fixed architectures and batch sizes; weight-decay and training-horizon ablations report training metrics. Reporting held-out metrics alone does not test these versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that warmup followed by monotonic decay is consistently effective on their neural-network workloads, flexible schedules offer generally small gains over standard cosine, and base learning-rate tuning matters more than detailed schedule shape. They also find that weight decay strongly affects optimal shape and qualify generality because they studied few small workloads.
record.recipe_differences: The study searches learning-rate schedule shapes on small CIFAR-10 and WikiText-103 training workloads; it does not reproduce the claim versions’ interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Schedule family and dataset change reported test metrics. The study also reports schedule-shape dependence on weight decay and training horizon, but those experiments primarily report training metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: In Figure 6, test-selected schedules reduce CIFAR-10 error from 0.283 for Constant to 0.260 for Cosine and approximately 0.258 for several flexible families. WikiText-103 perplexity falls from 28.5 for Constant to 26.5 for Cosine and 26.0–26.3 for flexible families.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate schedule shape affects the best test-selected performance attained on these small, optimization-limited AdamW workloads.

record.problems: Only three small workloads were studied. The authors note larger variation and fewer seeds/search points for WikiText-103; some runs with near-optimal schedules were unstable. The schedule-family comparisons do not directly measure train–test gaps.
record.rows_left_out: Training-metric schedule results, linear-regression results, and weight-decay, beta, and horizon ablations were left out because they do not report held-out generalization outcomes for a mapped version; the paper's related-work summaries are cited prior results.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe; chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test-error behavior as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or convolution-derived initialization.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Held-out effects of adding dropout, varying its strength or training-set size, or removing dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against other generalization measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. The decisive issue is the absence of the comparisons required by V1–V8, not simply the absence of a train–test-gap measurement. Figure 6 reports test-selected performance, so its values should retain that selection qualification.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance for the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum, including tuning and optimizer changes.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train–test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring its effect on test accuracy.
